# gtk4next is gtk4 placed in SNGL (TODO.md, Part 5): the program is calls of
# the platform's protocol functions, which GTK's C and the runtime's
# (lib/platform/gtk4next/rt) answer, C calling them as it calls C and Go
# through the wrappers cgogen writes, so a Go program has no cgo of its own.
# A click is the GLib signal a test emits, which reaches the closure through
# the runtime's trampoline, and a test's component is shown in a toplevel of
# its own.

sngl test --platform=gtk4next --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4next --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# gtk4next draws what gtk4 does, in both languages: gtk4's C records the
# snapshots, and gtk4next's are held to them.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c snap.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=
sngl test --platform=gtk4next --language=c snap.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4next --language=go snap.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

component main ui.node {
    var n = 0
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="clicked {n}")
        ui.button #count(text="{n}", @click {
            n += 1
        })
    }
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    main()
}

func testClickReachesTheClosure(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.count.click()
    c.count.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 2)
}
-- snap.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

component main ui.node {
    var n = 0
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="Count {n}")
        ui.button #inc(text="More", @click { n += 1 })
    }
}

ui.window(title="Counter") {
    main()
}

func testDrawsTheComponent(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.snapshot("zero")
    c.inc.click()
    t.snapshot("one")
}

func testDrawsTheWindow(t test.Test) {
    t.snapshot("whole")
}
